source.title: A neural network model of perception and reasoning
source.authors: Paul J. Blazek; Milo M. Lin

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper qualitatively compares interpretability in its custom essence neural networks (ENNs) and gradient-descent networks (GDNs), but it does not test the listed audit, scale, attribution-graph, or explanation-scoring claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative observations about neuron weights in ENNs and GDNs. These observations do not measure the share of neurons with one main job or test an independent explanation on held-out activations. Other results, such as task accuracy and robustness, do not bear on the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper builds essence neural networks (ENNs) whose neurons are constructed by design, via clustering and SVMs, to separate concepts. It then qualitatively shows that their weights are interpretable, while small gradient-descent networks (GDNs) show 'little to no intelligible structure'. It does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons in any trained model, study language models, InceptionV1 or attribution graphs, or score explanations on held-out activations. Interpretability here is imposed by construction, not measured as arising in ordinary trained networks. So none of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right but narrow. The authors also conclude that ENNs match GDN accuracy and training time, and are sparse and modular. They add that ENNs support symbolic manipulation and blind generalization (orientation, TSP, binary decision trees) and are more robust to noise and adversarial attacks. They present ENNs as a black-box-free approach and a framework for biological cognition.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes concept-based ENNs trained using clustering and SVMs; it does not reproduce the cited neuron-pole audit or explanation-scoring methods.

fits_no_version.finding: Small MLPs trained by gradient descent on MNIST and rectangles show little intelligible first-layer weight structure, unlike ENNs constructed from concept SVMs. ENN subconcept lesions remove class accuracy sequentially; GDN lesions do so haphazardly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small image MLPs, neurons constructed explicitly as concept separators are qualitatively more interpretable and modular than same-size gradient-descent neurons.

record.code_released: Code used in the project will be made available at a future date; no URL stated.
record.problems: The neuron-interpretability evidence is qualitative and tied to the paper’s custom ENN design and small image-task settings; it does not quantify interpretable-neuron shares or validate explanations on held-out activations.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported findings concern task accuracy, generalization, lesions, noise, and adversarial robustness; they do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and no shares of one-job, two-job or unknown neurons.
No language models, dense or MoE, at any scale.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose or recursive-generalization analysis.

ENN interpretability is built in by design. The GDN comparison is qualitative on small MNIST and rectangle MLPs and gives no interpretable-neuron shares. It tests neither regularization nor tools as causes, and gives no InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution graphs from a model's own neurons and no replacement-model comparison.
No test of explanations from activating examples against held-out firing.
No simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1–r4 correctly carry versions ['none']. Their qualitative weight-inspection evidence is about a custom construction method, not about neurons arising naturally in trained networks. The GDN rows (r2, r4) loosely bear on the general idea of messy gradient-trained neurons, but give no share or tool comparison relevant to V4.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or estimates of the shares with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
No audit across language models, model sizes, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.

The paper qualitatively contrasts its custom ENN architecture with GDNs but does not test the stated causes of messy late-layer neurons or estimate interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized models.
No attribution graphs built from a large model’s own neurons, or comparison with a trained replacement model and reconstruction error.
No test of whether explanations fit on activating examples predict where neurons fire on new activations.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
